label: neiso 50 head repro
definition: KEEPER SWAP (promoted 2026-07-06, replacing neiso-49-stgas-netload): byte-reproducible re-solve of the IDENTICAL neiso-49 recipe (same run_config, reliability-floor CSV, offer bands, flags) on current main HEAD, not a structural change. neiso-49's registered numbers rested on an uncommitted, never-captured WIP edit at solve time (git.dirty=true) that produced a spurious NEISO zonal price separation (HQ_import pricing $0.31-$1.86/MWh below the mainland zones); a git bisection across the full commit range back to the keeper's base commit, including a clean checkout of that base, confirmed the separation never existed in any committed state and was purely a WIP artifact of that one session. neiso-49's bundle and ablation twin have been retired. The honest, reproducible price level is correspondingly worse than neiso-49's (C3a demand-weighted price: 2023 -8.3% -> -10.4%, 2024 -7.8% -> -8.6%, 2025 -1.6% -> -4.4%); C1 fuel-mix and C3b shape are unchanged to reproducibility noise. Determination stays CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS (unchanged from neiso-49). D-3 UPDATE (2026-07-06): the previously owner-deferred zero-forcing ablation twin is now solved and registered (2026-07-06-neiso-50-ablation, bundle results/calibration/neiso49_resolve_confirm-ablation) and linked via this sidecar's "ablation_twin" field, clearing audit_keepers E9; see calibration_attestation.json exceptions (criterion: governance, RESOLVED 2026-07-06, was OWNER-DEFERRED (temporary)). Keeper-vs-twin per-class deltas are small (max +-0.17 TWh) — the fit is not floor-dependent (see market_story).
market_story: Floors buy almost nothing in NEISO (max class delta +-0.17 TWh vs the zero-forcing twin): COAL_BIT (Merrimack) runs its take-or-pay/seasonal commitment pattern rather than pure merit (-0.17 TWh without the floor in 2025); CC_CHP/CT_CHP steam hosts hold output for industrial steam load (-0.13/-0.06 TWh); CT_PEAKER absorbs the small backfill when those floors are off (+0.17 TWh). No class's floor buys more than 0.2% of ISO load - the NEISO fit is carried by fuel/passthrough physics, not commitment scaffolding.
